claims.text: The rider's own cancellation is not chargeable at all. The trip record shows accepted_at 18:10:00 and cancelled_at 18:11:30, a gap of 90 seconds, which is inside the 180-second grace after matching in force for this trip (platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec = 180). Under POL-NS-10(a) a rider's cancellation within that grace is not chargeable whatever the driver's position, and a driver's early arrival does not shorten the grace.

Because the cancellation is non-chargeable under POL-NS-10(a), POL-NS-10(c) requires the cancellation fee charged on it to be refunded in full with no driver compensation. The ledger records SGD 4.50 charged at 18:11:35 with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the entire contested sum is still with the platform.

The fee independently fails POL-NS-01 at limb (a): that limb requires a driver 'arrived' event in the trip record, and this record has none - arrived_at is null and the only events are driver_assigned at 18:10:00 and trip_cancelled at 18:11:30. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, so the failure of limb (a) alone defeats the charge and sends the refund question to POL-NS-02 to POL-NS-06 and POL-NS-10.

The driver's own trace puts him 667.17 m from the pickup pin on every one of the 10 fixes - min_distance_m equals max_distance_m equals mean_distance_m - so he was stationary and never came near the pickup. That is far outside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point. Under POL-NS-02 the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

The 667 m separation also takes this case outside POL-NS-03, whose wrong-entrance route applies only to stationary fixes outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin. Beyond 400 m the driver is treated as never having arrived and POL-NS-02 governs, so no wrong-entrance analysis can rescue this fee.

POL-NS-01 limb (c) is likewise unsatisfied. The waiting clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from any arrival tap, and the trace records qualifying_fix_count 0 with dwell_start_offset_sec null, so no continuous dwell of the 180-second free waiting period was ever served.

Measured as POL-NS-06 measures it, the effective in-geofence dwell is zero seconds - longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec is 0 and run_count is 0 - against a required minimum of 180 seconds for this STANDARD zone. The shortfall is the full 180 seconds, so the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

There is no traffic advisory on file for this pickup. EV-ADVIS-00852-01 is MISSING and carries weight_multiplier 0.0, and I disclose that impairment. Its absence is itself citable and it matters, because POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present and populated advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road. No such advisory exists, so the zero-second dwell cannot be excused or accumulated and the full refund under POL-NS-06 stands.

POL-NS-01 limb (d) is unsatisfied as well. That limb requires the trip to have been terminated by the driver under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, but this record shows cancelled_by RIDER with cancellation_reason_code null and no boarding event anywhere. A rider-initiated cancellation with no reason code is not a no-show termination and cannot support the fee.

On the only driver-profile fields this category permits to be used, the driver shows no anti-farming pattern at all: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 100, a rate of 0.01, far below POL-NS-07's conjunctive test of 4 or more terminations AND a rate above 0.08. Compensation cannot be withheld on that ground and POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged against this driver. The lifetime counters prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags that sit on the same profile are context only under POL-GEN-01 and may never be substituted for the trailing-window counters the clause actually names.

No false-arrival finding can attach to this driver, because there is no arrival marker to be false. The trip record's event list contains only driver_assigned at 18:10:00 and trip_cancelled at 18:11:30; the 'arrived' event POL-NS-05 operates on was never recorded, and the derived arrival facts return arrived_at as null. POL-NS-05 is therefore not engaged at all, and the false-arrival referral its limbs (ii) and (iii) direct is not available against him. The trace itself is clean: 10 driver fixes at the 10 second cadence, 100 percent coverage, no gaps, weight 1.0, no issue codes fired.

The trip ended by the rider's own election, on her own admitted error, and not by any act or omission of the driver. Her contemporaneous message at 18:10:20 reads 'I selected the wrong destination and need to cancel.', and the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER with status CANCELLED_BY_RIDER. Nothing in the record shows the driver terminating the trip, asking her to cancel, or a booking mismatch of vehicle or driver. The loss from the aborted trip originates in the rider's own destination entry, and no adverse conduct referral against this driver is supported by the record.

If any money is returned to the rider, it is confined to the cancellation-fee line the rider was actually charged. EV-FARE-00852 shows a single cancellation_fee of 4.50 SGD and a total_charged of 4.50 SGD, with no base fare, distance fare, time fare, surge, toll or waiting-time line, and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. POL-NS-06 directs that the cancellation-fee line be refunded and not any booking or platform fee that would have been charged on a completed trip, so the monetary exposure on this fare cannot exceed 4.50 SGD and cannot extend to the 6.61 SGD gross figure carried in platform_policy, which was never charged.

I do not contend that the driver arrived or that the fee is chargeable on performance, and I say so rather than stretch the point. The derived arrival facts record 0 qualifying in-radius fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds; the driver's stationary fixes sit 667.17 m from the pickup pin, outside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius POL-NS-02 sets and outside the 400 m ceiling that would bring POL-NS-03 into play, so POL-NS-02 governs and the driver never arrived. The trip record carries no 'arrived' event and no driver-termination reason code, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d) are not made out on this record and the POL-NS-07 payout is not engaged. My case on this trip rests on the three points above, not on a claim of arrival.

ruling.explanation: This dispute is decided on the cancellation-grace rule and the record's own arithmetic. The platform policy in force for this trip sets platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec at 180 seconds, so the cancellation fell well inside the grace period. Under POL-NS-10(a) a rider's cancellation within that grace is not chargeable whatever the driver's position, and a driver's early arrival does not shorten it; under POL-NS-10(c) the cancellation fee charged on such a cancellation is refunded in full with no driver compensation. Fare breakdown EV-FARE-00852 records exactly one charge — the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 (total_charged SGD 4.50, refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00) — so the whole contested sum of SGD 4.50 is returned to the rider. The no-show route does not rescue the fee. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and fails at every limb: there is no driver 'arrived' event in EV-TRIP-00852 (limb (a)); the driver's track in EV-GPS-00852 places him 667.17 m from the pickup pin on all ten fixes, so there is no qualifying in-radius fix under POL-NS-02 (limb (b)); the qualifying in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period (limb (c), POL-NS-06); and the record shows cancelled_by RIDER with cancellation_reason_code null and no driver termination for no-show (limb (d)). The 667 m separation also puts the case outside POL-NS-03's 400 m wrong-entrance window, so no wrong-entrance analysis applies; the driver's advocate properly conceded he does not contend arrival. On the driver's points: the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against 100 completed trips over 30 days, far below the conjunctive 4-or-more AND above-0.08 test — but that only clears the way for a payout, it does not create one, because POL-NS-10(c) expressly awards no driver compensation on a grace-period cancellation. There is no false-arrival marker to refer, because the record contains no 'arrived' event, so POL-NS-05 is not engaged and its false-arrival referral does not arise. The rider's own message at 18:10:20 ('I selected the wrong destination and need to cancel') confirms the trip ended by her election; no conduct referral against the driver is supported and none is made. Confidence: the deciding facts (the 90-second interval and the SGD 4.50 charge) are carried by EV-TRIP-00852 and EV-FARE-00852, both at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes, so the cap is 1.0 and the finding is well above the 0.70 escalation floor; no POL-NS-09 trigger fires. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically on issue, subject to appeal under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: No false-arrival finding can attach to this driver, because there is no arrival marker to be false. The trip record's event list contains only driver_assigned at 18:10:00 and trip_cancelled at 18:11:30; the 'arrived' event POL-NS-05 operates on was never recorded, and the derived arrival facts return arrived_at as null. POL-NS-05 is therefore not engaged at all, and the false-arrival referral its limbs (ii) and (iii) direct is not available against him. The trace itself is clean: 10 driver fixes at the 10 second cadence, 100 percent coverage, no gaps, weight 1.0, no issue codes fired.

The trip ended by the rider's own election, on her own admitted error, and not by any act or omission of the driver. Her contemporaneous message at 18:10:20 reads 'I selected the wrong destination and need to cancel.', and the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER with status CANCELLED_BY_RIDER. Nothing in the record shows the driver terminating the trip, asking her to cancel, or a booking mismatch of vehicle or driver. The loss from the aborted trip originates in the rider's own destination entry, and no adverse conduct referral against this driver is supported by the record.

If any money is returned to the rider, it is confined to the cancellation-fee line the rider was actually charged. EV-FARE-00852 shows a single cancellation_fee of 4.50 SGD and a total_charged of 4.50 SGD, with no base fare, distance fare, time fare, surge, toll or waiting-time line, and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. POL-NS-06 directs that the cancellation-fee line be refunded and not any booking or platform fee that would have been charged on a completed trip, so the monetary exposure on this fare cannot exceed 4.50 SGD and cannot extend to the 6.61 SGD gross figure carried in platform_policy, which was never charged.

I do not contend that the driver arrived or that the fee is chargeable on performance, and I say so rather than stretch the point. The derived arrival facts record 0 qualifying in-radius fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds; the driver's stationary fixes sit 667.17 m from the pickup pin, outside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius POL-NS-02 sets and outside the 400 m ceiling that would bring POL-NS-03 into play, so POL-NS-02 governs and the driver never arrived. The trip record carries no 'arrived' event and no driver-termination reason code, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d) are not made out on this record and the POL-NS-07 payout is not engaged. My case on this trip rests on the three points above, not on a claim of arrival.
